svg.text: Food rides on a silicone mat: a capstan nose feeds it to a blade or delivers it; one wall arm, a press and turntables do the rest.
1400 × 600 × 2100 mm (oven and ware washer outside) · ≤ 7.5 kW
est. cost: machine part ≈ €7.1 k (prototype ≈ €12.8 k) + oven
front strip: blade and press columns
THE MEAL: Frikadellen with mash, 4 persons
onion: halved at the blade, diced in the press
patties: mixed on P1, dished + pinned on mat S
mash: potatoes riced through the press
HOW THE FOOD FLOWS (active station highlighted)
mat S red (raw) · mat D green (dough, ready-to-eat) · moving parts orange · heat red

g.text: 1/8 Mat D is out. The box cradle tips an onion onto it; the capstan nose E feeds it to the blade, which lands on the anvil stick
2/8 The halves drop onto the moving mat; the arm winds the hem over the press tube on P1; the press pushes them through a 6 mm grid
3/8 The arm parks the hem of mat D; the mat runs back into its slot through the gate — sprays and squeegee wash it on the way
4/8 Mat S out, hem parked in the pocket fork. Mince from the cradle into the bowl; T turns it against a hung kneading frame
5/8 The arm portions the mass with the disher onto mat S, then rolls the ring-gauged pin over them: patties, 22 mm
6/8 The arm takes the hem; E feeds the patties over the nose; the arm moves the bar along the pan while winding: laid in a row on P3
7/8 Potatoes boiled in skin on P2: the arm tips the basket into the ricer tube on P1, the press rices them — the skins stay in the tube
8/8 Mat S is drawn back through its gate and steamed in its closed slot; plates leave through the right port
